messages.subject: How I can test my density estimation ? How analysed the lcl and ucl
messages.subject_clean: How I can test my density estimation ? How analysed the lcl and ucl
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm a student in Ecology and I'm working on monitoring of feral cat in New Caledonia during by camera trapping my internship.
I'm new on secr analysis but I want to learn how to use this for my study.

I've found conditions in the website of University of Otago to use secr but I want to have more details about the main conditions to use secr if it's possible.

I've producted this script :

library(secr) ## détails > ?secr

setwd("~/Stage Malik OEDIN 2015/Données/Chat/Stat/SECR")

catCaptHist <- read.capthist("catCapHist5.0.txt", "pointgps.txt", detector = "proximity") ## Chargement des fichiers

summary(catCaptHist) # Résumé de catCaptHist

## Mean Maximum Distance Moved
MMDM.catCaptHist<-MMDM(catCaptHist)
# MMDM is the average maximum distance between detections
# of each individual i.e. the observed range length averaged over individuals (Otis et al. 1978).
MMDM.catCaptHist

## Root Pooled Spatial Variance
RPSV.catCaptHist<-RPSV(catCaptHist)
# a simple measure of home-range size, Scalar distance in metres,
# or a list of such values if capthist is a multi-session list.
RPSV.catCaptHist

## Asymptotic Range Length
ARL.catCaptHist<-ARL(catCaptHist)
#  ARL is obtained by fitting an exponential curve to the scatter of
# observed individual range length vs the number of detections of each individual (Jett and Nichols
# 1987: 889).
ARL.catCaptHist

library(maptools)
library(GISTools)

setwd("~/Stage Malik OEDIN 2015/Données/Chat/Stat/SECR/boundary_zone_d_etude")
boundary_zone_d_etude<- readShapePoly ("boundary.shp")

polyarea(boundary_zone_d_etude)

plot(boundary_zone_d_etude)
str(boundary_zone_d_etude)

plot(catCaptHist,tracks=F,add=T) # Sans tracés
plot(catCaptHist,tracks=T,add=T) # Avec tracés -> track for repeat detections on same occasion joins points in arbitrary sequence

boundary_zone_d_etude@bbox
map.scale(x=497000, y=7638300,len=1000,ndivs=2,units="kilomètres",subdiv=0.5)
north.arrow(x=497890, y=7638220,len=100)

Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude<-make.mask(traps(catCaptHist),type="polygon",poly=boundary_zone_d_etude)
# vérification: plot(Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude)

setwd("~/Stage Malik OEDIN 2015/Données/Chat/Stat/SECR/boundary_zone_d_etude+Buffer_MMDM")
boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM<- readShapePoly ("boundaryMMDM.shp")

polyarea(boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM) # aire en hectare --> 1 ha = 0.01 km²

plot(boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM)
str(boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM)

plot(catCaptHist,tracks=F,add=T) ## Sans tracés
plot(catCaptHist,tracks=T,add=T) ## Avec tracés -> track for repeat detections on same occasion joins points in arbitrary sequence

boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM@bbox
map.scale(x=497000, y=7638300,len=1000,ndivs=2,units="kilomètres",subdiv=0.5)
north.arrow(x=497890, y=7638220,len=100)

Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM<-make.mask(traps(catCaptHist),type="polygon",poly=boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM)
# Vérification :plot(Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM)

#fit models conditional likelihood, compare the three different detection functions
#detectfn=0 is normal, 1 is hazard rate, 2 is exponential
catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d0<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=0,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude,CL=T)
catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d1<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=1,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude,CL=T)
catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d2<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=2,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude,CL=T)

## Comparaison des différents modèls par AIC
AIC(catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d0,catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d1,catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d2)

## SECR Model Predictions
# Evaluate a spatially explicit capture–recapture model. That is, compute the ‘real’ parameters corresponding
# to the ‘beta’ parameters of a fitted model for arbitrary levels of any variables in the linear
# predictor.
# Détails : ?predict.secr
predict(catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d0)

catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d0

derived(catCaptHist.fit.Mask_d0)

#fit models conditional likelihood, compare the three different detection functions
#detectfn=0 is normal, 1 is hazard rate, 2 is exponential
catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=0,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM,CL=T)
catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d1<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=1,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM,CL=T)
catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d2<-secr.fit(catCaptHist,detectfn=2,mask=Mask.boundary_zone_d_etude_MMDM,CL=T)

## Comparaison des différents modèls par AIC
AIC(catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0,catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d1,catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d2)

predict(catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0)

## Estimation de la densité et de l'Erreur Standart
derived(catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0)

I want to know what is exactly g0 and sigma ?
And how I can use lcl and ucl to know the strenght of my analysis ? Or what is the method to know the strenght of my analysis ?

Exemple of my results:

> predict(catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0)
       link    estimate SE.estimate         lcl         ucl
g0    logit   0.2473892  0.04018811   0.1771703   0.3341371
sigma   log 793.5134200 71.98419239 664.5000506 947.5748680
>
> ## Estimation de la densité et de l'Erreur Standart
> derived(catCaptHist.fit.MaskMMDM_d0)## Density = D = cat/ha -> 1 ha = 0.01 km²
        estimate SE.estimate         lcl        ucl       CVn        CVa       CVD
esa 1.217419e+03          NA          NA         NA        NA         NA        NA
D   1.560678e-02 0.003607299 0.009979846 0.02440636 0.2294157 0.02815259 0.2311366

Thank by advance for your help,

Malik OEDIN

messages.body_plain:
Hi Malik,

Most scientific papers using SECR give a basic description of g0 and sigma, I suggest you consult this classic paper http://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-0-387-78151-8_11

Regarding the ‘strength’ of the analysis, if you mean goodness-of-fit testing, this is still in development. The function secr.test() allows goodness-of-fit testing on full likelihood models but you are using conditional likelihood models.

However, I suspect you actually want to know how close your estimated parameters are to reality (i.e. accuracy). This could be assessed via simulation, but I suspect that would be excessive for your project. Here I would propose you draw on other ecological wisdom (or published studies) on your focal species to compare estimates, or if precision is your interest then assess the confidence intervals.

If you require more help, e-mail me directly, since application of SECR to predator studies on seabird islands is of particular interest to me, and I can direct you to colleagues in France who have applied SECR for island conservation. I’m always happy to help my friends on French islands achieve better conservation.

James
